• 2026-10-26

    Hacked target: Bloom Trading

    Description of the event: The cross-chain trading automation platform Bloom Trading suffered a security incident. Attackers exploited a Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability in a third-party module, draining approximately 9,408 SOL (about $947,000) from 49 wallet addresses belonging to 9 users. The team confirmed no private keys were compromised, other wallets remain safe, pledged full reimbursement to affected users, and temporarily paused some services while investigating.

    Amount of loss: $ 947,000 Attack method: Supply Chain Attack

  • 2026-10-25

    Hacked target: Yapeswap

    Description of the event: The Ethereum DeFi protocol Yapeswap (an AMM DEX) was hit by a governance attack. WorkersUnion’s zero-quorum setting allowed a proposal backed by only ~0.000055% of voting power to transfer YapeFactory’s feeToSetter role to the attacker. The attacker then installed a malicious Registry that made latestVault() return fake vaults while vaults() still listed real ones. YapePair counted the diverted deposits as farming assets without issuing redeemable shares, resulting in a loss of approximately $21,900.

    Amount of loss: $ 21900 Attack method: Governance Attack

  • 2026-10-21

    Hacked target: Fearless Wallet

    Description of the event: Polkadot issued a security alert stating that the Fearless Wallet browser extension (a third-party wallet) had been compromised since February 2025. Malicious code sent users’ private keys to an attacker-controlled server when the wallet was unlocked. Eight users have reported unauthorized transactions totaling 17,286 DOT. Affected users are urged to create new keypairs in a different wallet and move funds immediately.

    Amount of loss: $ 20000 Attack method: Private Key Leakage

  • 2026-10-14

    Hacked target: Pirate Chain

    Description of the event: A transaction validation vulnerability in Pirate Chain source code allowed the unauthorized creation of approximately 39.8 million ARRR, increasing the total supply by about 20%. The newly minted funds were transferred into the Sapling shielded pool. NonKYC identified suspicious deposits, restricted the associated accounts, and blocked withdrawals. The exploit combined two validation failures: bypassing the issuance check and incorrect interpretation of the output scripts. dPoW operators suspended notarizations as a precaution, and exchanges/pools were asked to pause operations while a recovery plan is developed.

    Amount of loss: $ 10,746,000 Attack method: Transaction Validation Vulnerability

  • 2026-10-09

    Hacked target: EtherVista

    Description of the event: EtherVista’s liquidity pool was exploited due to an integer overflow in the K-invariant check inside EtherVistaPair.swap(). Both reserves are uint112, so their product can wrap around and the check can pass even when the real reserve product drops sharply. The attacker registered a self-controlled contract as an authorized router and ran two crafted swaps to drain WETH and VISTA, with a loss of about $18,600.

    Amount of loss: $ 18600 Attack method: Smart Contract Vulnerability
